audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Cassiopeia Level 1, Level 2, Level 6 and 2+ items. The entry's own text says 'Level 1 is his', that level 2 is a stage where 'neither side clearly owns it yet', that at 6 'you rarely outright kill him', and that 'the lane flips back once he has two items'. Cassiopeia is at 48.53% over 68 games.
audit.why: Lane difficulty is a key point; the chart claimed four stages Cassiopeia does not win, including the late game the page explicitly concedes.
audit.corrected: Tryndamere / Skill / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia / Skill / Cassiopeia / Tryndamere in both layers.
sources: the entry's own spikes[0], spikes[3], whys[1] and late text

audit.whatIsWrong: Undying Rage is named as the matchup-defining cooldown in both layers with no duration, and Bloodlust is never mentioned at all.
audit.why: Power spikes is a key point. 'Make him spend R' is only a plan if you know it is 120s at rank 1 — that is the window you actually get to kill him in.
audit.corrected: Undying Rage quoted as 120s at rank 1 falling to 80s, Bloodlust as 12s, in the level-6 spike and the cooldown text.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mocking Shout is described as a tool to 'slow your kite and cut your auto damage'. Both halves read wrong for Cassiopeia: the attack-damage reduction does nothing to a champion whose damage is entirely abilities, and the slow only applies to enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere. Bloodlust's healing is never mentioned, so nothing on the entry tells you to buy Grievous Wounds.
audit.why: Point 4 is the most important point. Mocking Shout's back-turned condition is the difference between kiting facing him and being caught — and it is the one thing about that ability that matters to Cassiopeia.
audit.corrected: Mocking Shout restated as a slow that only lands with your back turned, with facing-him kiting as the counter, and its AD reduction dropped as irrelevant; Bloodlust's 12s heal tied to Grievous Wounds.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tryndamere.json (W: 'Enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere also have their Move Speed reduced'; Q Bloodlust heal)

audit.why: Riot's name is Twin Fang. The packet also flagged 'Use Serpentine Grace' as a suspect name — that is a false positive, Serpentine Grace is correct.
audit.corrected: Renamed in whys[2]; Serpentine Grace left alone.

edits.before: Petrifying Gaze (R) stuns him mid-spin to stop the all-in, but Undying Rage means he can't drop below 1 HP for 5s — you stun and kite, you rarely outright kill him through R.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze stuns him mid-spin to stop the all-in, but Undying Rage (120s at rank 1) holds him at 1 HP for 5s — stun and kite; you rarely kill through it, so make him spend R.

edits.before: Use Serpentine Grace move speed plus Q's speed buff on champion hit to walk out of his spin range and reset poke
edits.after: Mocking Shout only slows you with your back turned — kite facing him, then Serpentine Grace carries you clear of his spin

edits.before: Spinning Slash (E) onto you, crit-spin (Q) you down, and use Mocking Shout (W) to slow your kite and cut your auto damage
edits.after: Spinning Slash (E) onto you and crit you down, then Mocking Shout (W) to slow your kite the moment your back is turned

edits.before: Stack crit and lifesteal (IE, Phantom Dancer) so his spin out-sustains your poison and out-DPSes your single-target Twin Fang
edits.after: Stack crit and lifesteal so his spin plus Bloodlust (12s) out-heals your poison — without Grievous Wounds you lose the grind

edits.before: Full Q-to-E poison chain plus the Miasma ground comes online — lock his Spinning Slash in place and chain Twin Fangs through an extended trade he can't win.
edits.after: Full Q-to-E poison chain plus the Miasma ground comes online — lock his Spinning Slash in place and chain Twin Fang through an extended trade he cannot win.

edits.before: - Tryndamere Undying Rage: matchup-defining — Five seconds unkillable — save your kill damage for after it ends. Check it before every step-up. - W Miasma is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Tryndamere Undying Rage: matchup-defining — 120s at rank 1, 80s maxed; save your kill damage for after the 5s ends. - Bloodlust is 12s and heals off Fury, so bring Grievous Wounds. - W Miasma is the lifeline; chip never gets it.

notes: UNVERIFIED: this entry's central claim — that Miasma's grounding shuts off Spinning Slash — is left in place, but champ-data/_kits/tryndamere.json carries NO dash flag on E (its flags array is empty), so the kit file does not confirm it. Riot's own description, 'slices toward a target unit', reads as a movement ability and grounding disables movement abilities, so this is very likely a derived-flag misfire rather than a content error. Worth one wiki check before the applier trusts nine strings that depend on it. Note also that whys[2] as edited still asserts it.
